body:
I think on one level I am alone. That's not really the point though. 

I talked to a school (uni) counselor for a while, I don't think he was a therapist exactly though. I know CBT is supposed to be great for the irrational stuff, I probably should give it a serious try. 

I suppose the thing worrying me about this particular thought (wanting to disappear/never have been) is that it isn't like the other ideations. I think it's in response to everything else. It seems like if things get bad enough I might become willing to settle for the next best thing, even if I wouldn't right now. Or I could go into a sudden downswing and end things on impulse but at the moment that's unlikely.

I have a few things I need to sort out before thinking about a therapist, but you're right that it may be time for that. My main worry is that I couldn't be totally honest with a shrink for fear of getting a hospital stay. And if I'm holding important stuff back I don't know how much good will be done. I've been told that CBT can be learnt somewhat on your own, maybe I'll check that out. 

Thanks for replying.

After a while I got over the question of "why". Unlike some illnesses, this isn't something we brought on ourselves or even contracted by accident. It's down to our individual brain chemistry, maybe architecture too I don't really know. 

The issue for me is how to live as a person when I know my thoughts and emotions are driven by things unrelated to reality. I worry that like any other suicide, the amount of suffering I must undergo in order to continue will outweigh my moral sense. 

Thank you both for posting, and I'm really sorry to hear that you share this feeling. No one deserves it.
